\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بانک} (bânk)}{بانک (bânk)}]{\fa{بانک} (bânk) — a bank}

\label{lesson:FA-C70-bank}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for left, then the Persian for a street.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بانک}}
\textbf{\fa{بانک}} — \emph{bânk} — \textquotedblleft{}a bank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bânk} is borrowed from French \emph{banque}, \textquotedblleft{}bank\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). The French word goes back to Italian \emph{banco}, \textquotedblleft{}bench\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bânk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bânk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for left, then the Persian for a street, then say \emph{bânk} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ایستگاه} (istgâh)}{ایستگاه (istgâh)}]{\fa{ایستگاه} (istgâh) — a station, a stop}

\label{lesson:FA-C70-istgah}

Before the new one: say the Persian for a street, then the Persian for a bank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ایستگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{ایستگاه}} — \emph{istgâh} — \textquotedblleft{}a station, a stop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{istgâh} is built from \emph{ist-}, \textquotedblleft{}stand\textquotedblright{} (the stem of \emph{istâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{gâh}, \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}standing place\textquotedblright{}. Both parts are native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قطار} (ghatâr)}{قطار (ghatâr)}]{\fa{قطار} (ghatâr) — a train}

\label{lesson:FA-C70-ghatar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a car, then the Persian for a bus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قطار}}
\textbf{\fa{قطار}} — \emph{ghatâr} — \textquotedblleft{}a train\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghatâr} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{qiṭār}, \textquotedblleft{}line of camels\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{q-ṭ-r} (Lane). Lane describes camels tied one behind another; Persian moved the word to the train.
\end{cousinweb}
